title: Removing the last bit of an all-true word
statement: For every natural number $n$, cutting the word of $n+1$ true bits at its last true bit returns the word of $n$ true bits.
replaced: For a bit string $v$, let $\mathrm{split}(v)$ be the prefix of $v$ preceding its last occurrence of $1$, undefined when $v$ contains no $1$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{split}(1^{n+1})$ is defined and equals $1^n$, where $1^k$ is the word of $k$ ones.
